chose: The language adapter is one interface of five questions: resolve a named thing to a definition, list its references, report visibility (whether the language enforces it and whether the thing is visible outside its module), turn a via value into a test filter, and refute by opening a synthetic unsaved document; a Pyright adapter is a second file implementing the same five
over: an adapter that exposes raw protocol calls (workspace/symbol, textDocument/references) for enforcement to compose
enforcement calling the TypeScript compiler API in-process
because: enforcement should ask only the questions it has; raw protocol calls leak language specifics (import syntax for the synthetic document, what exported means) into the language-neutral check, and the journal decision d-b675d370 already fixed the protocol over the compiler API

chose: A spec value resolves as a symbol only in three forms: a bare identifier, <identifier> in <file suffix>, or a project-relative path to a module file; any other value (prose, a parenthesized name inside prose, two names) grades not chokeable with the message that the totality oracle form is the compromise
over: extracting an identifier from prose, such as the parenthesized (currentHost) in Mnemion's instance-identity host bullet
taking the first capitalized token
because: a guessed symbol would grade a claim the author never made; a not-chokeable verdict is honest and names the fix, which is to write the symbol

chose: A reference site on an import or re-export line is classified as an import, counted but neither inside nor a bypass
over: treating an import line outside the chokepoint as a bypass
dropping import sites silently
because: an import only brings the name into scope; the use it enables is its own reference site and is classified on its own, so counting the import as a bypass would grade every cross-file chokepoint broken

chose: One run record carries one entry per enforcement (component, invariant, form) rather than one entry per invariant with both forms folded in; the status view and the state derivation take the latest entry per (component, invariant, form)
over: one entry per invariant with form: both
because: a bullet may carry a chokepoint and a totality oracle as separate evidence paths, and each has its own verdict, refutation, and latency; folding them loses which one failed

chose: typescript-language-server is pinned to ^5.3.0 as an optional dependency, with typescript ^5.9.3 beside it
over: typescript-language-server 6.0.0, the current release
because: 6.0.0 declares engines node >=22.22.2 and this machine runs 22.21.1, so npm drops the optional install silently and the adapter would find no binary; 5.3.0 speaks the same protocol

chose: The adapter starts typescript-language-server with useSyntaxServer: never, one semantic tsserver only
over: the default pairing of a syntax server with the semantic one
because: workspace/symbol and textDocument/references were routed to the partial-semantic syntax server, which knows open documents only: a bare name resolved to nothing and references missed every closed file, which would have made every chokepoint look clean

chose: A protected thing that is not exported is refuted by an unsaved edit of its own module (didChange appending one use, then restored), since the language refuses an import from a sibling document
over: skipping the refutation for not-exported things and trusting the compiler
opening a synthetic sibling document anyway and reporting the miss
because: the compiler enforces the choke across modules, but the chokepoint claim is about references inside the module too; the in-module edit is the only synthetic site the instrument can be asked about, and a miss there would still mean a vacuous check

chose: When the protected thing is a module, references inside that module's own file are inside the chokepoint; when it is a symbol, a same-file reference outside the chokepoint symbol's range is a bypass
over: same-file references always inside
same-file references always bypasses
because: the glossary says module privacy is the unit when several members of one module legitimately touch the protected state, while a symbol claim names one site; Mnemion's writeClass claim is exactly the second case, and its own module references KERNEL_WRITE_POLICY from five other functions

chose: PostToolUse re-checks the chokepoint invariants whose latest run touched the written file or whose protected or chokepoint name appears as a token in the file's text, and appends a run record for that partial pass
over: re-checking every chokepoint invariant at every edit
re-checking without recording, so only a full run writes a record
because: a reference to a symbol needs its name in the file's text, so the token test is a cheap and honest pre-filter that needs no server; the partial pass is a run like any other, and the status view already keeps a skipped enforcement's prior dated verdict

chose: At the edit, when the instrument cannot run, the hook prints one line saying so as additionalContext rather than staying silent
over: silence, to keep the edit loop quiet
because: a silent alarm is a vacuous check; the agent must know the chokepoint was not checked, and the line costs nothing when the server is up

chose: A structural defect in the latest run makes the bullet's state structural defect whatever else it lacks, and the counts subtract it from requirements
over: structural defect only for a bullet that was an invariant before the run
because: the reveal is the point: a requirement whose declared chokepoint is already bypassed must alarm the same way, and the lacks are still listed beside it

chose: The warm server's socket lives under .coherence/run/adapter.sock when that path fits the platform limit, else under the system temp folder, with .coherence/run/server.json naming it either way
over: always under .coherence/run/
always under the temp folder
because: macOS caps a unix socket path near 104 bytes and a worktree under .claude/worktrees already exceeds it; the pointer file keeps the project folder the one place a client looks

chose: Mnemion's specs are left untouched: the fourteen prose protects: values grade not chokeable with the fix named, and the two claims that resolve (kernel write boundary, facet/kernel-column collision) are reported broken as written
over: rewriting prose protects: values as the symbol they mention, such as KERNEL_TABLES in schema.ts or currentHost
widening the two broken claims' chokepoints to their modules so they grade reference-choked
because: none of the names is wrong, they are prose; a symbol I pick changes what the claim protects, and widening a chokepoint to its module changes what the claim asserts; both are the owner's calls, and the honest verdict is the tool's whole point

observation: Mnemion's kernel write boundary claim (protects KERNEL_WRITE_POLICY, chokepoint writeClass) has five bypasses in policy.ts and schema.ts; the claim as written was never structurally true, since consentPolicy, primeIncluded, isAuditExempt, findUngatedCredentialMints, and verifyWritePolicyTotality all read the registry
couldBe: the intended protected thing is the write-class decision, so the chokepoint should be the policy.ts module with KERNEL_WRITE_POLICY not exported and schema.ts routed through a function
the claim should drop to the totality oracle form alone, which it already carries
discriminatedBy: the owner reading the five sites: if each is a legitimate reader of the registry, the module is the unit; if schema.ts:1270 is the only outsider, one function fixes it

observation: Mnemion's facet/kernel-column collision claim (protects KERNEL_COLUMNS in kernel-columns.ts, chokepoint FACET_RESERVED_COLUMNS) has two bypasses, both in kernel-columns.ts itself (KERNEL_COLUMN_SET and without)
couldBe: the chokepoint is the kernel-columns.ts module; with chokepoint: entities/Hive/kernel-columns.ts the claim grades reference-choked
the protected thing is misnamed and the claim is really about FACET_RESERVED_COLUMNS' completeness, which the totality oracle covers
discriminatedBy: running the check with chokepoint: entities/Hive/kernel-columns.ts; a clean pass says the module is the unit

chose: run exits 1 when any enforcement fails (a bypass, a missing chokepoint, a failing totality oracle) and 0 otherwise, so a not-chokeable or not-run verdict does not fail the command
over: exit 1 on any verdict other than pass
because: a structural defect is what the command exists to surface and belongs in an exit code; a prose protects value is a spec to improve, and failing the whole run on it would push adopters to delete the claim rather than sharpen it

chose: run --no-server drives the adapter in-process for one command; the hook and the default run always go through the warm server
over: no in-process path at all
because: the cold latency has to be measurable and tests need an adapter they own; the edit-time path stays on the server, which is the requirement

what: Measure at-the-edit latency on a repository the size of posthog/posthog, the case the warm server exists for
because: only Mnemion (about 150 source files) is on this machine; there the cold project load is under a second and a warm full pass is under 300 ms, which does not exercise the case

what: Run the Pyright adapter against anything: it is a stub by design in this slice
because: no Python project is an adopter yet and the slice fixes TypeScript first; the stub exists so the ladder's top rung is adapter-defined from day one

chose: The totality oracle pass runs every named test in one runner invocation with a combined name pattern and a per-test JSON report (config testJson, jest-shaped output), mapping results back by test name; one test per invocation is the fallback when a runner cannot report per test, and each run entry records which mode ran
over: one runner invocation per named test, as first built
because: the owner's ruling: per-test setup is a known failure of the reference. Mnemion's workers pool costs about 27 s per vitest start, so 29 named tests took about half an hour one at a time; the batched pass pays the setup once

what: Measure a full per-test totality oracle pass over Mnemion as a baseline
because: the owner ordered it terminated a quarter of the way through rather than paid for; the evidence in hand is a bare vitest start of 765 ms through npm exec against about 27 s per named test under Mnemion's workers pool (two measured: 26.8 s and 26.3 s), so 29 named tests would have cost about half an hour

chose: Before a re-check, the adapter opens and closes every file it touched since the last check plus the file the edit hook names, so tsserver reloads them from disk at once
over: trusting tsserver's file watcher to refresh a closed file
because: tsserver reads a never-opened file from disk and refreshes it only when its watcher fires, which is asynchronous; a check right after a write saw the old text and graded a repaired bypass still broken in one of two test runs, and closing a document is the one protocol act that makes tsserver reload it immediately
